paper.title: LiteCUA: Computer as MCP Server for Computer-Use Agent on AIOS
paper.central_claim: Turning the computer into an LLM-native contextual environment (computer as MCP server: screenshot + accessibility-tree perception, constrained atomic action space, sandboxed VM controller) decouples interface complexity from decision complexity; LiteCUA, a simple orchestrator-worker perceive-reason-act agent on AIOS 1.0, reaches 14.66% on OSWorld (Screenshot + A11y tree), above GPT-4o-based Friday, Open-Interpreter and AgentStore.

provenance.session_note: actual_model taken from the worker system prompt (Sonnet 5.5, claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]); no session id / receipt exposed to the worker, so null

materials.note: Short HTML render (36,351 chars) read in full; no appendix or ablation section exists in this version text. Figures 1-4 are not in the text.

evidence.quote: we introduce LiteCUA , a lightweight computer-use agent built on AIOS 1.0 that achieves a 14.66% success rate on the OSWorld benchmark, outperforming several specialized agent frameworks despite its simple architecture.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result and claim.

evidence.quote: we identify a fundamental limitation: the semantic disconnect between how language models understand the world and how computer interfaces are structured.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: conceptual, no measured failure analysis.

evidence.quote: Screenshot to provide visual signals and Accessibility Tree to provide structural information within the the current screen.
evidence.support_explanation: Perception channels of the MCP server.

evidence.quote: the action space is constrained into atomic but essential computer-related operations including CLICK, SCROLL, TYPE, DRAG, etc.
evidence.support_explanation: Constrained action space; actions are executed through pyautogui.

evidence.quote: a button is represented not merely as a visual element but as an interactive component with specific usage semantics
evidence.support_explanation: Perceptor restructuring of elements into semantic descriptions; construction method (rules vs LLM) not specified.

evidence.quote: to specific GUI control commands leveraging pyautogui
evidence.support_explanation: Actor module executes coordinate commands (not element-id actions).

evidence.quote: The Orchestrator serves as the central planning and coordination module, responsible for decomposing complex tasks into manageable subtasks, tracking progress toward goal completion.
evidence.support_explanation: Orchestrator role; no role-removal ablation.

evidence.quote: Considering that some of the computer-use operations can lead to irreversible outcomes, we design the VM controller to allow agents to reason and act in a safe sandbox.
evidence.support_explanation: VM controller / HTTP interface; sandbox rationale.

evidence.quote: we also provide the mechanisms to inspect invisible information like the version information of softwares.
evidence.support_explanation: Extra non-visual state channel (not evaluated).

evidence.quote: In LiteCUA , we deliberately design a perceive-reason-act cognitive cycle
evidence.support_explanation: Fixed loop; no memory/reflection/verification described.

evidence.quote: For a fair comparison, we evaluate all the methods under the "Screenshot + A11y tree" setting and only compare agents which do not introduce extra models for grounding.
evidence.support_explanation: Observation setting fixed to Screenshot+A11y; unclear whether baselines were re-run or cited.

evidence.quote: three agent baselines which adopt GPT-4o as their backbones, i.e., Friday ( 37 ) , Open-Interpreter ( 21 ) , and AgentStore ( 13 )
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline list; LiteCUA's own backbone is never stated in the text.

evidence.quote: Gemini-1.5-flash ( 31 )
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline list says Gemini-1.5-flash ...

evidence.quote: Gemini-1.5-pro ( 31 ) | 5.1
evidence.support_explanation: ... while Table 1 says Gemini-1.5-pro (internal inconsistency).

evidence.quote: AgentStore ( 13 ) | 13.55
evidence.support_explanation: Closest baseline: 13.55 vs LiteCUA 14.66.

evidence.quote: LiteCUA | 14.66
evidence.support_explanation: Headline number.
54.10/369 = 14.66%; fractional per-task score; average 35.3 steps.
Fractional score cell (partial-credit scoring not explained).

evidence.quote: Libreoffice Calc | 0/47 | 50.0
evidence.support_explanation: Zero-success domains with step budget exhausted (50.0).

evidence.quote: The maximum step count (50.0) in these domains indicates that the system exhausts its operation budget without achieving the task goals.
evidence.support_explanation: Implies a 50-step cap that is never stated explicitly.

evidence.quote: with a slight edge over AgentStore (13.55%)
evidence.support_explanation: Author acknowledges the margin is slight.

evidence.quote: Compared to GPT-4o (11.21%), our approach demonstrates that properly contextualizing computer environments for LLMs can yield better results than using the model in isolation.
evidence.support_explanation: Causal reading from a cross-system comparison; no same-loop ablation.

evidence.quote: the overall modest success rates across all systems (below 15%) indicate that computer-use tasks remain challenging for current AI systems
evidence.support_explanation: Author hedging.

evidence.quote: isolated VM with 2 AMD Ryzen CPU cores
evidence.support_explanation: Single deployment environment disclosed.

evidence.quote: UFO2 ( 49 ) designs and implements the desktop agent OS within the Windows environment.
evidence.support_explanation: Only mention of the closest 'agent OS / structured control' neighbour; not compared.

evidence.quote: By decoupling interface complexity from decision complexity, AIOS 1.0 addresses a fundamental bottleneck in current CUA capabilities.
evidence.support_explanation: Central mechanism claim; untested by ablation.

signatures.object: The agent-computer interface: observation representation, action space and VM control channel (baseline: raw screenshots/a11y tree and unconstrained pyautogui)
signatures.information: Screenshot, accessibility tree, and non-visual software information; no privileged labels, test data or future frames.
signatures.operation: Wrap the VM behind an MCP server that exposes perceived state and a constrained atomic action set encoded as JSON schemas; an HTTP VM controller isolates execution; Perceptor restructures elements into semantic descriptions.
signatures.output: LLM-readable state and schema-validated actions converted to pyautogui commands.
signatures.conditions: Accessibility tree must expose the targets; canvas-like or complex productivity UIs are harder (Calc 0/47, Thunderbird 0/15).
signatures.feedback: none beyond the next observation (no reflection or verification module described)
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable: static platform design; no candidate selection or retention
signatures.persistence: not_applicable: no stored experience or learned state
signatures.claimed_effect: Reduces interface complexity so a simple agent reaches 14.66% on OSWorld, exceeding other GPT-4o frameworks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Budget exhausted (50 steps) in Calc/Thunderbird; multi-app 11/101.

signatures.object: LiteCUA agent loop: Orchestrator + Perceptor/Reasoner/Actor workers
signatures.information: Same screenshot+a11y observation; operational rules in prompts (not shown).
signatures.operation: Orchestrator decomposes the task and tracks progress; Perceptor builds a structured description; Reasoner emits thought + action; Actor executes.
signatures.output: One action per step until completion or step budget.
signatures.conditions: Backbone model, prompts and step budget are not specified in the text.
signatures.failure_boundary: Context switching across apps (multi-app 11/101) and complex productivity UIs.

gap.author_gap: CUA research improves agent frameworks or models but ignores the environment: LLMs cannot natively interpret human-oriented interfaces, so an agent-specific contextualised environment is needed.
gap.checked_gap: A reasonable framing but not substantiated: no measurement of where raw screenshot/a11y inputs fail, and no comparison with prior agent-computer-interface designs that already restructure observations (Agent S ACI, UFO/UFO2 UIA+vision hybrid, SoM/OmniParser-style parsers). The paper's own related work names UFO2 only as 'agent OS' context.
lineage: Prompted LLM computer agents on OSWorld (GPT-4o baselines, Friday, Open-Interpreter, AgentStore) -> structured agent-computer interfaces / agent OS (AIOS, UFO2) -> AIOS 1.0 MCP contextualisation + LiteCUA

gap.residue: Whether the MCP-style contextualisation itself (vs the specific prompts, backbone or loop) produces any gain is unknown.
gap.stakes: If the wrapper adds no gain over a plain a11y+screenshot prompt, the platform claim reduces to an engineering integration.
gap.method_response: MCP-server abstraction, constrained atomic actions, VM controller, orchestrator-worker perceive-reason-act loop.
gap.remaining_gap: Causal evidence, specification of Perceptor/Reasoner prompts and schemas, backbone identity, failure recovery, and comparison to existing ACI designs.
unresolved: Neighbour sources other than UFO2 are not pinned locally; UFO2 was only skimmed (targeted lines) for lineage, so closest-adjacent comparison is incomplete.
LiteCUA backbone model is not stated in the text, so the 'fair comparison' to GPT-4o agents cannot be verified.

rs_pattern.reason: Candidates read in full: unify_into_shared_representation (no single shared model/objective replaces per-modality pipelines; screenshot and a11y tree remain separate inputs wrapped by a schema), architectural_operator_substitution (no cheaper surrogate and no preservation argument), decompose_and_delegate (orchestrator/worker roles are all LLM prompts; no sound external solver or verified handoff artefact). The operation is an interface/engineering abstraction (agent-computer interface redesign) that none of the 15 original definitions describes, so primary=null; the paper is still fully scored.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: not claimed by any pattern; the stated problem (semantic disconnect) is not shown to be closed (no ablation).

condition_checks.reason: C14 evidence is an ablation of action pruning (AgentOccam); LiteCUA constrains actions to CLICK/SCROLL/TYPE/DRAG but reports no ablation of the action space.
Step inflation/untested removed actions: average 35.3 steps, budget exhausted in Calc/Thunderbird; no comparison to a richer action set.
Perceptor restructures a11y elements into semantic descriptions, but no rule-based pruning, token-savings, or success-vs-observation comparison is reported.
Parsing cost and per-site losses are unreported.
Each role removed with the same backbone: no role-removal ablation.
No role-removal ablation and per-step cost unreported.

unassigned: MCP server as an abstraction over VM state and actions has no direct card; planner_grounder_interface/K29 (action-interface redesign) is the nearest family but K29 requires tagged elements or a tool library, which LiteCUA does not use (actions are coordinates via pyautogui).
revision_proposals: none: single weakly-specified system paper; no second independent source for an 'MCP/ACI platform' candidate_pattern

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Domain C14: prune/simplify the prompted agent's action space. LiteCUA states its action space is 'constrained into atomic but essential' operations and encodes them through pyautogui.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: C14's evidence is an ablation on WebArena; LiteCUA reports none. The mapping is descriptive only; there is no original-card counterpart (outside_taxonomy).

claims.text: LiteCUA scores 14.66% on OSWorld, outperforming Friday (11.11), Open-Interpreter (8.94), AgentStore (13.55) and GPT-4o alone (11.21).
claims.setting: OSWorld 369 tasks, Screenshot + A11y tree, isolated 2-core/4GB VM
claims.baseline_control: GPT-4o-mini/GPT-4o/Gemini baselines and three GPT-4o frameworks; provenance of baseline numbers not stated
claims.selection_vs_test: no development/test separation described; no training
claims.counterevidence: LiteCUA's backbone is unstated; single run; 1.1 pp over AgentStore; Gemini naming inconsistency (flash vs pro).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported single-run 14.66% on OSWorld in the Screenshot + A11y setting; superiority over baselines is not established.

claims.text: Contextualising the computer as an MCP server decouples interface complexity from decision complexity and yields better agent performance.
claims.counterevidence: No same-loop raw-interface baseline; the cross-system comparison confounds architecture, prompts and backbone.

claims.text: A simple orchestrator-worker perceive-reason-act design suffices for competitive CUA performance.
claims.counterevidence: Zero success in two applications with budget exhaustion; authors call overall rates modest.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Simple design reaches a modest rate; sufficiency/competitiveness not shown.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: OSWorld execution-checked results (author-reported); no held-out or cross-platform evidence and no description of selection/test separation.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: The authors report 14.66% (54.10/369) single-run success on OSWorld in the Screenshot + A11y setting for a simple agent built on their platform; whether the MCP contextualisation causes this, and whether it beats other GPT-4o frameworks, is not established.
not_supported: Superiority over Friday/Open-Interpreter/AgentStore beyond a 1.1 pp single-run margin
unresolved: Baseline numbers' provenance and step budgets
assessment.retention_trace: not_applicable: static system, no retained or self-improving component claimed

G.reason: Gap is conceptual ('semantic disconnect') without a measured failure mode, and prior structured agent-computer interfaces (Agent S ACI, UFO/UFO2 UIA hybrid, parsers) are not examined as nearest neighbours; residual problem boundaries are not stated.

M.reason: MCP-style contextualisation is described at slogan level; how the Perceptor derives 'usage semantics', what the JSON schemas contain and why they should beat a plain a11y+screenshot prompt are not reconstructable, and no distinguishing prediction is offered.

X.reason: Component names and the perceive-reason-act cycle are given, but backbone, prompts, schemas, step cap, history handling, error recovery and verification are all unspecified; the loop is not reproducible from the text.

E.measurement.reason: OSWorld's execution-based evaluation is a trusted verifier, but the harness fidelity, fractional scores, unnamed backbone, uncited baseline provenance and an internal Gemini inconsistency leave the reported numbers hard to audit.

E.causality.reason: No ablation or controlled comparison isolates the contextualisation (raw vs MCP input with the same loop/backbone), the orchestrator-worker roles or the perception channels; the only support is a cross-system leaderboard-style comparison.
